market.summary: Indian markets gave up most of a strong open but still closed higher: Sensex +0.46% to 84,328.59, Nifty +0.25% to 25,884.50, with small caps (+0.74%) ahead of large caps. IT led (+3.66%) and FMCG lagged; crude near $90-95 and West Asia tension capped the rally. The rupee slipped to about 92.40 in the morning on crude and the US tariff proposal, while FIIs stayed buyers. US markets were shut for Thanksgiving, so there is no US lead tonight; Friday is a short US session.

points.text: Sensex closed up about 390 points (+0.46%) at 84,328.59 and Nifty up about 65 points (+0.25%) at 25,884.50; Nifty Midcap 100 +0.32%, Smallcap 100 +0.74%.
Nifty IT was the best sector (+3.66%; HCL Tech, TCS, Infosys, Tech Mahindra among top gainers) and FMCG the worst (-0.94%); Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance were among the losers.

Rupee fell about 20 paise to 92.40 per dollar in early trade after its best close of the year (92.20) on Wednesday: higher crude and the US proposal of up to 25% tariffs on Indian goods (17% with a deal); FIIs bought a net Rs 4,479 Cr on Wednesday.
NYSE and Nasdaq were closed on 26 Nov for Thanksgiving; Friday 27 Nov is a short session (8:00-11:30 pm IST).

market.watch: Friday's thin US session and any Indian response to the US tariff proposal; crude above $90 is the main risk for the rally.
